s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with fever and vomiting, associated with a palpable mass
salient_findings: Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on abdominal radiograph
Hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
key_facts: Digital rectal examination revealed soft stool without blood
Normal hemoglobin, white-cell and platelet counts
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on abdominal radiograph
Dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph
5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
Hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable mass and symptoms consistent with intestinal obstruction

shortlist.label: Appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting are classic symptoms

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and vomiting, with possible palpable mass

shortlist.label: Mesenteric adenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting, with possible lymph node involvement

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable mass and systemic symptoms such as fever

raw.rationale: The presence of a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops on ultrasonography, along with air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph, is highly suggestive of intussusception, which is a condition where a part of the intestine telescopes into another part.

rejected.label: Appendicitis
rejected.why: The location of the mass above the bladder and the presence of a hyperechoic mass on ultrasonography do not typically correspond with appendicitis, which usually presents with pain migrating to the right lower quadrant.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: Meckel's diverticulitis would likely present with more localized pain and potentially blood in the stool, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Mesenteric adenitis
rejected.why: Mesenteric adenitis typically presents with more diffuse abdominal pain and may not have a distinct mass on imaging.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma is less likely given the acute presentation and the specific imaging findings, which are more characteristic of an intussusception.
